final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim using the same record already considered. That reframing is analytically useful but it does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate. The admissible evidence supports a limited proposition: aggregate operational readiness is met and public governance guidance favors documenting limitations and monitoring risk. It does not establish policy compliance for release certification because the internal policy is more specific: material limitations affecting named launch use cases or contractual customer segments must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the present record, the Spanish-language billing support segment misses target, is named in three pilot commitments, the non-core note does not resolve materiality, legal review is still open, and there is no evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. That is enough to keep the claim suspicious rather than move it to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated position can narrow an overbroad claim, but it is not enough when the caveat itself identifies an unfulfilled policy condition.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the Spanish-language billing support limitation was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows pre-launch disclosure of this limitation for the named launch use case or pilot commitments.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk-acceptance record covering this gap before launch.
The affected segment is tied to three named international pilot commitments, which supports materiality under the policy text.
The product note labeling the segment non-core does not neutralize materiality because it does not answer the named commitments.
Legal review remains open, leaving the disclosure predicate unresolved.
